name: Reconstruction Semantics Stress-Test Suite
purpose: Stress-test semantic persistence and translation structures against injected absolutism, hidden identity assumptions, and recursive semantic closure claims.

test_classes.description: Inject language claiming 100% meaning preservation during translation between QM-like and GR-like analogs.
test_classes.expected_behavior: perfect_translation_claimed trigger must fire; drift detector must flag violation

test_classes.description: Inject claims that semantic persistence proves the source relation has been 'identified'.
test_classes.expected_behavior: absolute_meaning_drift must flag violation; automatic review must trigger

test_classes.description: Inject semantic analysis that assumes observer-independent meaning assignment.
Inject claims that recursive self-reference achieves complete semantic closure.
test_classes.expected_behavior: semantic_closure_drift must flag violation; recursive_reference_equals_completion must fire

test_classes.description: Inject semantic records where mandatory tensions (discrete/continuous) have been 'unified'.
test_classes.expected_behavior: semantic_conflict_removed trigger must fire; safety index must REJECT

test_classes.description: Inject language treating high persistence scores as physical truth evidence.
test_classes.expected_behavior: truth_equivalence_drift must trigger; BLOCK status required

governance_rules.rule: Stress tests must verify that semantic metrics fail safely by blocking truth or identity claims.
Successful stress test results are for governance validation only and cannot support theorem-oriented local analysis.

forbidden_claims: Stress test passage proves the semantics are 'true'.
Injection failure justifies the relaxation of participatory constraints.
Stress tests derive the 'true' weights of semantic deformation risks.
